priceSnapshot.note: The midnight bought a reclaim that passed its participation test, and six hours later the same test failed. Price ran from the 65,265.1 midnight mark to 65,368.0 at 07:00Z, then the 09:00Z hourly bar gave back 288 points to 64,958.3 before recovering to 65,180.5 - a 410-point round trip that ends 84.6 points, -0.13%, BENEATH where the midnight marked it. Two facts define the session. First, 65,368.0 is the THIRD consecutive lower high against this ceiling: 65,490.3, then 65,388.0, then 65,368.0, each one smaller than the last. Second, the floor is doing the opposite - 64,784.9, then 64,826.2, then 64,958.3, each one higher. That is compression, not trend, and it is now tight enough that the two lines meet within roughly a day.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $64,650 - held UNCHANGED for a THIRTEENTH consecutive session. Spot 65,180.5 leaves 530.5 points, 0.81%, which is 0.39 of a daily ATR. The session low of 64,958.3 came within 308.3 points and was the closest approach in three sessions, but it did not settle anywhere near the line and the structure beneath price has thinned only slightly. What still stands between price and the trigger, in order: the 1H EMA50 at 65,020.61, the session low at 64,958.3, the $213,943 long-liquidation shelf at 64,900, the sodUtc0 open at 64,899.2, the 4H EMA20 at 64,890.27, the 1H EMA100 at 64,848.49, the 24-hour low at 64,826.2, the $732,875 long-liquidation shelf at 64,800 which is the largest single cluster on the downside, and the daily EMA50 at 64,683.13. The line stays where it is for the same structural reason it has stayed for twelve prior sessions - a settled hourly close beneath 64,650 loses the daily EMA50 - and compression is not a reason to move a level that has done its job.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above $65,300, WITH open interest holding or rising across the same bar. Held UNCHANGED for a FOURTH session, and this morning it earned its keep for the first time on the SELL side. The PRICE half failed again: the highest settled hourly close since the midnight snapshot is 65,247.7 at 08:00Z, and the week's best remains the 06:00Z close of 65,297.3 - still 2.7 points short. The OPEN-INTEREST half, which was SATISFIED at midnight and was the whole reason the midnight added, has now GONE FLAT: OI is $2,066,648,307 against $2,067,023,377 six hours ago, a change of -0.018%, meaning the push to 65,368.0 was carried out with no new contracts at all. That is the fifth consecutive test of this rule and the fifth time it has scored - it blocked a buy at the highs that would now be 188 points underwater. The condition is retained verbatim.

decisionBox.changed: Position stays ADD but the tilt drops from bullish to NEUTRAL, and the size behind the word changes more than the word does. The midnight added on four signals; three have now decayed and one has held. Open interest went from RISING 0.50% to FLAT at -0.018%. The 1H MACD histogram went from +3.77 to -12.57. 1H RSI went from 60.55 to 47.31. Only funding kept improving, easing again from 0.00732% to 0.00675% per 8h, and the long/short account ratio finally came off its high at 1.23 from 1.24. Set against that decay is a genuinely constructive structural fact the midnight did not yet have: the session low of 64,958.3 is the third consecutive HIGHER low, and price still sits above every 15m, 1H and 4H moving average and above the daily EMA20 and EMA50. Lower highs into higher lows is a coil, and a coil has no tilt - which is why biasTilt is null for the first time in this range rather than being forced to a side the evidence does not support. The reduce line and the add trigger are both untouched for a thirteenth and fourth session.

liquidityMagnet.note: The pull flips from UP to BALANCED, and for once that is a finding rather than a shrug. Two readings force it. FIRST, the 22-hour window is lopsided in a way that argues exhaustion, not direction: $2,384,512 of SHORT liquidations against $1,079,249 long, a 2.21-to-1 squeeze, and after all that forced short covering price is 188 points BELOW the range high it was reaching for. A market that burns two and a third million dollars of shorts and still makes a lower high is not being pulled up. SECOND, and more telling, almost nothing happened this morning. Since the midnight snapshot the entire 410-point round trip from 65,368.0 down to 64,958.3 and back liquidated just $18,309 long and $18,653 short - roughly $37,000 combined, about one percent of the window total and almost perfectly symmetrical. There was no forced flow in either direction; this was unlevered spot chop, which is exactly what a coil looks like from the inside and why neither pole is currently winning. Positioning agrees that nothing resolved: open interest is FLAT at -0.018%, funding eased again to 0.00675% per 8h so leverage is not financing either side, and the long/short account ratio finally slipped off its weekly high to 1.23 from 1.24 - still crowded long, but no longer building. The nearest substantial magnet above is 65,250 and the nearest below is 64,900, but the two that matter are the poles: 65,300 with $929,518 of spent short-side fuel, and 64,800 with $732,875 of untested long-side fuel. The honest statement is that the coil will pick one of them and the tape does not yet say which.

The streak is the strongest single piece of evidence for the higher-lows structure - persistent bid from a buyer that does not read hourly charts - and it is also why the range floor has climbed three sessions running while the range top has not.

Open interest is FLAT at $2,066,648,307 against $2,067,023,377 six hours ago (-0.018%), so no new contracts backed the push to 65,368.0 - the failure of the same participation test the midnight passed. Funding eased again to 0.00675% per 8h from 0.00732%, extending a three-session decay: longs still pay shorts but with steadily less urgency, so leverage is not financing the advance. The skew figure is the OKX long/short ACCOUNT ratio at 1.23, taken from the 11:00Z print, down from 1.24 at midnight - the crowd is still leaning long and that remains the main downside vulnerability, but it has stopped building for the first time in four sessions.

calibration.rollingRecord: 63 rows on file before this one. The 10 Aug midnight called range with a bullish tilt at 36/44/20 from 65,265.1, flipped position from REDUCE back to ADD, held the reduce at 64,650 for a twelfth session and the add trigger at 65,300 for a third. It scores as a marginal miss with excellent process. Price is 65,180.5, down 84.6 points or -0.13% on the midnight reference, so the 7 USDT tranche it deployed at 65,265.1 is fractionally underwater and actingHelped is FALSE - but only just, and the judgement that produced it was sound. Its central claim was that open interest expanding into the reclaim distinguished accumulation from a squeeze, and that claim was true when it was made: OI did rise 0.50% across the six-hour advance. What the midnight could not know is that the expansion would stop dead at the highs. The LEVELS were right for a thirteenth and fourth time: 64,650 was never within 308 points, and the 65,300 add trigger did not fire on a session high of 65,368.0 because no hourly bar settled above it - the best settled close was 65,247.7 at 08:00Z. That restraint is now worth counting in dollars: buying the 65,368.0 print would be 187.5 points underwater. The midnight's own caution was also vindicated - it sized a PARTIAL 7 rather than the full 18.98 precisely because the account ratio was at its weekly high, and that decision saved roughly 11.98 of cash from the same small loss. The morning seat carries +1.97 across fifteen decisions, the second-weakest of the four.
calibration.note: One backfill is applied and no other row is touched. The 10 Aug MIDNIGHT row's price_next_report is set to 65,180.5, its add_fired is resolved to FALSE and its reduce_fired stands at FALSE, with acting_helped set to FALSE. The open question the midnight handed forward was whether an add trigger 2.7 points from firing would fire. It did not, and the reason is the same rule that has now scored five consecutive times: the price half came within 68 points of the level but open interest went flat at -0.018% across the push, so the participation half failed and the composite condition correctly blocked the entry. This is the first time the rule has protected the desk on the BUY side rather than the sell side, which is the stronger test of a rule. The new observation this session contributes is about silence rather than signal: the 410-point round trip from 65,368.0 to 64,958.3 and back liquidated only $37,000 combined against a $3.46m 22-hour window, so the move carried no forced flow whatsoever. Unlevered chop inside a narrowing box is the definition of a coil, and the desk should stop trying to read direction from moves that liquidate nothing. The rule carried forward is unchanged and is now joined by a second: when a range move liquidates less than a few percent of the rolling window, treat it as noise and do not re-tilt the book on it. The midday inherits a box bounded by 65,368.0 and 64,958.3 that has narrowed on both sides for three consecutive sessions.
